text:
benchbot: PR 14720 CI microbench failure: kernel-selection.test +6.8% (threshold 3%). Job: https://ci.internal/runs/8201
arian: saw the alert, thanks. Is it p50 or tail?
benchbot: summary:
- p50: +2.1%
- p95: +5.9%
- p99: +12.4%
- total tokens/sec: -4.6%
sasha: ugh p99 jump. That smells like a kernel coldstart or different kernel chosen for some seqlen/batch combos.
mohit: pulling the PR diff now. Looks like kernel_selector heuristic changed in abc1234 -> tweak to prefer stable kernels for long sequences.
mohit: running local harness: `./dev/bench --test kernel-selection --seqlen 512 --batch 8`
arian: any chance this only hits the allocator path? I remember a change to prefetching last week.
mohit: quick paste of failing flamegraph (truncated):
```
flamegraph.svg -> hot path: fallback_kernel::init -> cudaMemcpyAsync -> kernel_launch_overhead
previous: optimized_kernel::dispatch -> smaller launch overhead
```
sasha: so selector now chooses fallback_kernel for seqlen 512+batch8 where before it chose optimized_kernel. fallback has higher per-launch overhead, cheaper per-token later. For microbench short traces it regresses tail.
linh: starting a bisect on CI jobs to see which commit flip happened. kicking off bisect job 8202.
ci-bot: bisect job 8202 queued (owner: linh). steps: 12, expected ~18m.
arian: can you reproduce the flip locally by forcing the selector to return candidate X vs Y? e.g. set ENV KSEL_FORCE=optimized_kernel and run.
mohit: forced run: with KSEL_FORCE=optimized_kernel -> p99 down to baseline (-0.8%). With forced fallback_kernel -> reproduces +13% p99. So confirmed selector choice is root cause.
mohit: diff snippet of the change (from PR 14720):
```
- // prefer opt if cost_ratio < 0.85
- if cost_ratio < 0.85 { choose = Optimized } 
+ // favor stability: bump threshold
+ if cost_ratio < 0.92 { choose = Optimized }
```
sasha: hmm bumping threshold made more cases choose optimized? Wait that reads inverted. Might be a sign error (we saw more fallback chosen).
mohit: yep looks like a sign bug in comparison after refactor. On top of that the selector's warmup counter was reset in some paths so the runtime thought optimized_kernel was unready.
linh: bisect result (8202): culprit commit abc1234 (PR 14720), matching mohit's observation.
release-manager: marking PR 14720 as rollout-blocker and holding merge window. @arian @mohit please prepare revert or fix.
mohit: opening revert PR now -> revert commit def5678. quick bench after revert (local): kernel-selection.test p99 -0.9%, p95 -1.4%, tokens/sec +2.3%
benchbot: CI run for revert PR 14720-revert: job 8205 completed: microbench diffs within noise: p99 -0.6%, overall -0.3%.
release-manager: thanks, roll forward the revert while we investigate proper fix.
sasha: long-term fix: add unit test for selector truth table and add a microbench that covers seqlen distribution (128/256/512) to catch tail regressions. Also add an assertion for warmup counter not being reset on code paths.
mohit: agreed. I'll open PR to reintroduce change with tests and fix sign + warmup bug. Targeting PR 14721.
arian: nice catch. Can we also add a CI gate that runs kernel-selection microbench in the PR perf-suite so we fail faster?
release-manager: yes, add to perf-gate for post-merge for this component. For now, revert stays.
linh: bisect artifacts: https://ci.internal/bisect/8202/artifacts (contains pprof, traces, selector logs)
mohit: note for the fix: prefer explicit enum decisions over floating threshold math; it's too easy to invert.
sasha: small followups: log chosen kernel in prod with sample rate 0.1% for next week so we can monitor real traffic distribution.
arian: ok tagging this thread in the revert PR. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
benchbot: note: automated alert suppressed for PR 14720 while revert in flight.
release-manager: cc @eng-runtime-product — holding release until check passes.
ci-bot: thread closed automatically after revert merged (job 8205).
